sports.name: Soccer
sports.subtext: Men's & Women's · D1, D2, D3, NAIA
sports.positionsExample: goalkeepers, center backs, outside backs, holding mids, and strikers
sports.rosterFitProfile: position, graduation year, height, test scores, club or school pathway, home and travel distance, and budget
sports.rosterFitFactors: seven factors: room at your athlete's position, academics, roster make-up, your pathway's level, height, distance and cost
scenario: Say your athlete is a 2027 center back. Open a program and RosterWise lays out the whole picture — not a schedule and a coach's email, but the roster itself.

You see the center backs already there and their class years, so you know whether a spot opens in your athlete's window or whether they'd sit behind two returning juniors — and the size and physical profile the program actually recruits at the position, so you know whether your athlete fits inside it.

You see where the roster is built from — the states and countries, the specific clubs and academies its players came through, and how much of it is international — so you can tell whether your athlete's pathway is one this staff already trusts. You see whether the program reloads through high-school recruiting or the transfer portal, and how long the head coach has been building it.
And you see the school behind the team: its academic strength, size, campus setting, and how well it graduates its students — because fit is academic, not just athletic.
Then My RosterFit™ checks all of it, athletic and academic, against your athlete: a light for each factor and one fit band, Strong, Good, Mixed or Weak, for every program on your list.

sports.name: Lacrosse
sports.subtext: Men's & Women's · D1, D2, D3, NAIA · NJCAA (men's)
sports.positionsExample: attack, midfield, defense, goalie, and LSM
sports.rosterFitProfile: position, graduation year, height, test scores, home and travel distance, and budget
sports.rosterFitFactors: six factors for men's programs (room at your athlete's position, academics, roster make-up, height, distance and cost) and five for women's, without roster make-up
scenario: Say your athlete is a 2027 attackman. Open a program and RosterWise gives you the whole picture instead of a name on a bracket.

You see the attackmen on the roster and their class years — how many graduate before or during your athlete's window, and how many would still be ahead of them — plus the listed heights at the position.

You see where the roster is built from: the states and countries, and the last school each player lists — club, prep school, high school, or a previous college — so you know whether your athlete's background fits. You see which players arrived as transfers, from the previous colleges their roster entries list, and how long the head coach has been there.
And you see the school itself: its academic strength, size, campus setting, and how well it graduates its students — the part of the decision that lasts four years, not one season.

Then My RosterFit™ checks room at your athlete's position, academics, location, cost, and the rest of the fit picture, and gives every program you're considering one fit band, Strong, Good, Mixed or Weak, with the reasons behind it.

scenario: Say your athlete wrestles 149. Open a program and RosterWise answers the question that actually decides fit — who wrestles 149, and when do they graduate? — and then keeps going.
You see who's stacked at the weight and their class years, so you know whether a lineup spot opens in your athlete's window rather than guessing from a schedule.

You see the program's recruiting geography and the high schools and clubs its wrestlers came through, whether it builds through high-school recruiting or the transfer portal, and how long the head coach has been building the room.
And you see the school behind the singlet: its academic strength, size, campus setting, and how well it graduates its students — because a wrestling career is four years and a degree is forever.

Then My RosterFit™ checks room at your athlete's weight class, academics, distance and cost, and gives every program on your board one fit band, Strong, Good, Mixed or Weak, with the reasons behind it.
